submission.reasoning: An elevated cmd.exe (proc-690e6c933a), run by WORKSTATION5\wardog on workstation5, ran sc.exe three times. At 00:45:33 sc.exe (proc-f4d3576242) pointed the Fax service binPath at 'powershell.exe -noexit -c write-host T1543.003 Test'. At 00:45:35 'sc start Fax' (proc-cd222a569d) started the service, and a PowerShell process (proc-7f9f3418e9) ran as NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE with that command line, so the hijack worked and the command ran with service privileges. At 00:45:41 a third sc.exe (proc-babd722e6c) set binPath back to fxssvc.exe. This matches MITRE ATT&CK T1543.003 (modifying a Windows service to run code), and the payload text suggests an Atomic Red Team style test. It is still a real service hijack that ran code, so the verdict is malicious. The Fax service configuration needs checking even though it appears to have been reverted, and the account used should be rotated.
